note: Comparison inputs. Prices are as listed on the access date, in the seller's currency; nothing was ordered. The radio transmitter, goggles and charger are needed by every option and are left out of every row.

strategies.name: Buy a sub-250 g GPS micro long-range BNF
strategies.identity: Flywoo Explorer LR 4 V2.2 analog BNF with GPS (4-inch, 1404 2750KV, GOKU stack)
strategies.price_alt_note: same item shown sold out on a collection page
strategies.takeoff_mass_note: Flywoo lists about 229 g takeoff for the O4 Wide version with its 4S 750 mAh pack; the analog V2.2 figure was not reached.

sources.supports: 278.49 USD regular price; 239.99 USD sold out on a collection page; GPS; 1404 2750KV
O4 Wide: about 162 g without battery, about 229 g with Flywoo 4S 750 mAh; 359.99 USD; GOKU GM10 Mini V3 GPS about 4.5 g

strategies.for: Cheapest path to a flying GPS sub-250 g aircraft; tuned by the maker; no fabrication risk.
strategies.against: No HS design content: the integration loop the mission asks for (sizing, stack, UART map, frame, payload mount) is done by the vendor. Payload mounting is whatever the frame allows.

strategies.name: PX4/Pixhawk open development kit
strategies.identity: Holybro PX4 Development Kit X500 v2 (Pixhawk 6C, M10 GPS, 915 MHz telemetry)
strategies.takeoff_mass_note: Kit weight without battery per Holybro; a 4S 3000-5000 mAh pack adds several hundred grams.
strategies.flight_time_note: Holybro: about 18 min hover, no payload, 5000 mAh

sources.supports: 609.00 USD; 610 g; about 18 min hover with 5000 mAh; 1500 g payload at 70 % throttle; 16x16 / 19x19 motor mounts

strategies.for: Best autonomy stack and the largest payload of any option; mature open firmware and documentation.
strategies.against: Over the 250 g line before the battery is fitted (ratio computed below), so registration and larger-prop hazards apply; costs more than any other option; needs an outdoor field for every test.

strategies.name: Closed nano reference (existing System Example 001)
strategies.identity: Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1+ with an HS sensor deck (PR #230/#231)
strategies.price_note: Not on the Bitcraze product page; the 2026-11-13 audit gives 'about US$240 bare' from store and RobotShop listings.

sources.supports: 29 g takeoff; 92 x 92 x 29 mm; 7 min; 15 g max payload

strategies.for: Excellent firmware and sensing testbed; already integrated in this repository.
strategies.against: A finished product, indoor-only, with the smallest payload and endurance in the table. It does not answer 'from obtainable parts'.

strategies.name: 65 mm printed whoop build (PR #276 / #291)
strategies.identity: HS65 printed frame + BETAFPV Matrix 1S 5-in-1 + 0702 motors + Gemfan 1210-2
strategies.against: Corrected build minimum is above the cheapest BNF; FDM frame is heavier than the PP and printed frames it replaces; payload is zero; governing thrust number unpublished.

strategies.name: Custom sub-250 g 3-inch GPS quad (this package)
strategies.identity: HS-3G: HS-generated carbon frame + SpeedyBee F405 Mini stack + 4x F1404 3800KV + HQ T3x3x3 + M10Q-5883 + 4S 650 mAh, INAV or ArduPilot

sources.supports: every part identity, mass and price

strategies.for: Every engineering variable is HS's to set and check; open firmware with GPS return-to-home; payload mass and mount are designed in; parts are commodity and individually replaceable; the method carries to a 5-inch.
strategies.against: Costs more than the GPS BNF (section 5 decision); nothing about it has been built, weighed or flown.
